Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 52, verses 1–6:

(p-5540) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Tur

Al-Mahayimi said: It was named so because it contains the glorification of the place of descent of revelation (mahbit al-wahy). Revelation is most worthy of glorification, so concern with action is magnified, especially since the ascent of action (mis'ad al-'amal) and its fruit have become great. This is among the greatest aims of the Qur'an. It is Meccan, and its verses number forty-nine.

Al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and Malik narrated from Jubayr ibn Mut'im, who said: "I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) recite Surah al-Tur in the Maghrib prayer, and I never heard anyone with a more beautiful voice or recitation than his."

Al-Bukhari narrated from Umm Salama, who said: "I complained to the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that I was unwell. He said: 'Circumambulate behind the people while you are riding.' So I circumambulated while the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was praying beside the House, reciting: 'By the Tur, and a Book inscribed.'"

(p-5541) In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[1–6] ﴿By the Mount (al-Tur)﴾ ﴿and a Book inscribed﴾ ﴿on parchment unrolled﴾ ﴿and the frequented House﴾ ﴿and the raised canopy﴾ ﴿and the sea filled with fire (al-masjur)﴾.

﴿By the Mount (al-Tur)﴾: that is, the Mount of Sinai (Tur Sinin), a mountain in Madyan, where Musa, may God's blessings be upon him, heard the speech of God, exalted is He, and it was crumbled by the light of His manifestation, exalted is He.

﴿and a Book inscribed﴾: that is, written. What is meant by it is the Qur'an, or what encompasses the revealed books.

﴿on parchment unrolled﴾: this is connected to ﴿inscribed﴾, meaning: a Book that was written on unrolled parchment which is read out to the people openly. (Al-raqq) is the sheet or the skin on which one writes.

﴿and the frequented House﴾: that is, the one that is made populous by the abundance of those who visit it, which is the Ka'ba, frequented by pilgrims, the 'umar (those performing 'umra), those who circumambulate, those who remain in devotion, and those who dwell near it. It is reported that it is a house in the heavens directly above the Ka'ba on earth, which seventy thousand angels enter every day, and then they never return to it again. The first (view) is more apparent, because it corresponds with what came in Surah al-Tin regarding the conjunction of the "secure city" with "Mount Sinin," and the Qur'an explains one part of it by another, due to the similarity and close resemblance of its verses, even though the eloquence of its style varies.

(p-5542) Al-Mahayimi said: He placed it after the Book, which is revelation, because it is the locus of the greatest actions intended by it, and because it is the manifestation of revelation and the source of the general mercy sent to the worlds; and because it is the most majestic and greatest of the signs, as indicated by the verse ﴿Have they not seen that We made a sanctuary secure, while people are snatched away from around them?﴾ [al-'Ankabut: 67] and other verses.

﴿and the raised canopy﴾: meaning the heaven; and He made it a canopy because it is for the earth like the roof of a house, which is its ceiling.

﴿and the sea filled with fire (al-masjur)﴾: that is, filled up, or that which is kindled, i.e., becomes fire. Like His saying ﴿and when the seas are set ablaze (sujjirat)﴾ [al-Takwir: 6]. Ibn Jarir said: The first (meaning) is preferable, I mean: its meaning is the sea that is full, its water gathered one part into another; because the more common meanings of (al-sajr) are kindling or being full. When the sea is not kindled today, the second attribute, which is fullness, is established for it, since at every time it is full. And do not forget what we mentioned at the beginning of (al-Dhariyat) that these oaths are all indicators brought forth in the form of faith.

The interpretation of His saying, may He be exalted:

[7–16] ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is going to occur﴾ ﴿there is none to avert it﴾ [al-Tur: 7–8] ﴿on the Day when the sky will sway violently﴾ [al-Tur: 9] ﴿and the mountains will move away [in motion]﴾ [al-Tur: 10] ﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers﴾ [al-Tur: 11] ﴿who are, in their discourse, playing around﴾ [al-Tur: 12] (p-5543) ﴿On the Day they are pushed toward the fire of Hell, forcefully﴾ [al-Tur: 13] ﴿"This is the Fire which you used to deny"﴾ [al-Tur: 14] ﴿"Is this magic, or do you not see?"﴾ [al-Tur: 15] ﴿"Burn in it, and be patient or be impatient; it is the same for you. You are only being recompensed for what you used to do."﴾ [al-Tur: 16]

﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is going to occur﴾ ﴿there is none to avert it﴾ [al-Tur: 8] meaning: none will repel it from the deniers, so as to rescue them from it when it befalls.

﴿on the Day when the sky will sway violently﴾ [al-Tur: 9] meaning: it will be agitated.

﴿and the mountains will move away [in motion]﴾ [al-Tur: 10] meaning: they will move away from the surface of the earth, and become scattered dust.

﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers﴾ [al-Tur: 11] meaning: those who deny the truth and reject it.

﴿who are, in their discourse﴾ [al-Tur: 12] meaning: in the sense of plunging recklessly and mocking, ﴿playing around﴾ [al-Tur: 12] meaning: with the signs of God and His proofs.

﴿On the Day they are pushed toward the fire of Hell, forcefully﴾ [al-Tur: 13] meaning: they will be shoved into it with violence. It is said: "I pushed him in the back" (dada'tu fi qafāhu) when you thrust him forcefully with agitation.

﴿"This is the Fire which you used to deny"﴾ [al-Tur: 14] meaning: this is what will be said to them.

﴿"Is this magic"﴾ [al-Tur: 15] meaning: that which you have now encountered. The fa' (the particle fa, here) indicates causation, since this is caused by what they said about the revelation. ﴿"or do you not see?"﴾ [al-Tur: 15] meaning: just as you did not see in the world. Al-Zamakhshari said: he means, "Or are you blind to what is reported, just as you were blind to the news," and this is rebuke and mockery.

﴿"Burn in it"﴾ [al-Tur: 16] meaning: taste the heat of this Fire. ﴿"and be patient"﴾ [al-Tur: 16] meaning: over its pain. ﴿"or be impatient; it is the same for you"﴾ [al-Tur: 16] meaning: both matters, patience and its absence, are the same for you. ﴿"You are only being recompensed for what you used to do."﴾ [al-Tur: 16] meaning: you will only be punished for your disobedience to your Lord in the world, and your disbelief in Him.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, why did he give as the reason for the equality of patience and its absence his saying, "You are only being recompensed..."? I say: because patience has merit over impatient lament only for its benefit in the outcome, by which the patient one is rewarded with good recompense. But patience over the punishment, which is itself the recompense, has no outcome and no benefit, so it has no merit over lament.

You are only being recompensed for what you used to do."﴾ [al-Tur: 16]

﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord is going to occur﴾ ﴿there is none to avert it﴾ [al-Tur: 8] meaning: none will repel it from the deniers, so as to rescue them from it when it befalls.

﴿on the Day when the sky will sway violently﴾ [al-Tur: 9] meaning: it will be agitated.

﴿and the mountains will move away [in motion]﴾ [al-Tur: 10] meaning: they will move away from the surface of the earth, and become scattered dust.

﴿Woe, that Day, to the deniers﴾ [al-Tur: 11] meaning: those who deny the truth and reject it.

﴿who are, in their discourse﴾ [al-Tur: 12] meaning: in the sense of plunging recklessly and mocking, ﴿playing around﴾ [al-Tur: 12] meaning: with the signs of God and His proofs.

﴿On the Day they are pushed toward the fire of Hell, forcefully﴾ [al-Tur: 13] meaning: they will be shoved into it with violence. It is said: "I pushed him in the back" (dada'tu fi qafāhu) when you thrust him forcefully with agitation.

﴿"This is the Fire which you used to deny"﴾ [al-Tur: 14] meaning: this is what will be said to them.

﴿"Is this magic"﴾ [al-Tur: 15] meaning: that which you have now encountered. The fa' (the particle fa, here) indicates causation, since this is caused by what they said about the revelation. ﴿"or do you not see?"﴾ [al-Tur: 15] meaning: just as you did not see in the world. Al-Zamakhshari said: he means, "Or are you blind to what is reported, just as you were blind to the news," and this is rebuke and mockery.

﴿"Burn in it"﴾ [al-Tur: 16] meaning: taste the heat of this Fire. ﴿"and be patient"﴾ [al-Tur: 16] meaning: over its pain. ﴿"or be impatient; it is the same for you"﴾ [al-Tur: 16] meaning: both matters, patience and its absence, are the same for you. ﴿"You are only being recompensed for what you used to do."﴾ [al-Tur: 16] meaning: you will only be punished for your disobedience to your Lord in the world, and your disbelief in Him.

Al-Zamakhshari said: If you ask, why did he give as the reason for the equality of patience and its absence his saying, "You are only being recompensed..."? I say: because patience has merit over impatient lament only for its benefit in the outcome, by which the patient one is rewarded with good recompense. But patience over the punishment, which is itself the recompense, has no outcome and no benefit, so it has no merit over lament.

[21] ﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith — We will join their offspring with them, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds. Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned.﴾

﴿And those who believed and whose offspring followed them in faith﴾ means: they followed their footsteps in faith and righteous deeds. ﴿We will join their offspring with them﴾ means: in the Gardens and in bliss. The address is to what was with the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, who were certain of Allah's promise. He completed for them the glad tidings of what was promised, that it would reach their offspring too, if they followed their fathers in goodness. This is the intended meaning of the verse. As for the one who said regarding its meaning that the believer will have his offspring raised up to him so that they join him, even if they were below him in deeds, the verse does not indicate this either explicitly or allusively. ﴿And We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds﴾ means: We will not diminish from the reward of their deeds anything. ﴿Every person is held in pledge for what he has earned﴾ means: he is held in pledge by what he has done of good or evil. No one is taken to account for the sin of another; rather, a person is punished only for his own sin.

[29] ﴿So remind, for you are not, by the favour of your Lord, a soothsayer (kahin) nor a madman.﴾

[44] ﴿And if they should see a piece of the sky falling down, they would say, "Layered clouds."﴾

The discussion of the words of Allah, the Exalted:

[47] ﴿And indeed, for those who have done wrong is a punishment short of that, but most of them do not know.﴾

﴿And indeed, for those who have done wrong is a punishment short of that﴾ i.e., short of the Day of Resurrection. The wording is true of all of them. ﴿But most of them do not know﴾ i.e., the sunnah (way/custom) of Allah concerning the likes of them among the wicked (al-fajara).

The Explanation of His Words, Exalted is He:

[48] ﴿And be patient for the judgment of your Lord, for indeed you are under Our eyes, and glorify your Lord with praise when you arise﴾

﴿And be patient for the judgment of your Lord﴾ That is, the judgment He has decreed upon you. Proceed with His command and prohibition, and convey His messages.

(p-5550) ﴿For indeed you are under Our eyes﴾ Ibn Jarir said: That is, in Our sight. We see you and see your deeds, and We protect and safeguard you, so that no harm reaches you from those among the polytheists who intend you evil.

Al-Shihab said: The meaning is that the eye, because of the protection and guarding it provides, has been borrowed for that purpose, and also for the guardian himself, just as the sentry (al-rabi'ah) is called "eye" (ʿayn), and this is a well-known and eloquent usage. The reason for using the plural (ʿuyun, "eyes") here and the singular in the story of the Speaker with God (Musa), apart from the fact that it is plural here because it is attached to a plural pronoun while it is singular there because it is attached to a singular pronoun, is hyperbole in protection, as if with Him there were a group of guardians watching over him with their own eyes. This is because the intent is to make His beloved steadfast against plots and the hardships of obligations and obedience; thus the plural is appropriate, since these are many acts, each of which requires a guard, indeed guards. This is unlike what is mentioned there regarding the safeguarding of Musa, peace be upon him. ﴿And glorify your Lord with praise when you arise﴾ That is, from your sleep.

Imam Ahmad narrated from ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, from the Messenger of God (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever wakes up during the night and says: There is no god but God alone, with no partner; to Him belongs the dominion and to Him belongs the praise, and He is capable of all things. Glory be to God, praise be to God, there is no god but God, God is greatest, and there is no power nor might except through God. Then he says: My Lord, forgive me, or he said: then he supplicates, he will be answered; and if he resolves and performs ablution and then prays, his prayer will be accepted." Al-Bukhari included it in his Sahih, and so did the compilers of the Sunan.

Among the remembrances upon waking from sleep is the saying: Glory be to God and praise be to Him; glory be to God, the Holy One. And: There is no god but You; glory be to You, O God, I seek Your forgiveness for my sin, and I ask You for Your mercy. O God, increase me in knowledge, do not let my heart deviate after You have guided me, and grant me mercy from Yourself; indeed You are the Bestower.

It has also been said: "when you arise" means when you rise for prayer. Muslim narrated in his Sahih from ʿUmar that he would say at the beginning of the prayer: "Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You, blessed is Your name, exalted is Your majesty, and there is no god other than You." Ahmad and the compilers of the Sunan narrated it from Abu Sa'id and others, from the Prophet (ﷺ), that he "used to say that." And from Mujahid: "when you arise" means from every gathering. Likewise said ʿAta' and Abu al-Ahwas.

Abu Hurayrah narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Whoever sits in a gathering in which much idle talk occurs, and before he rises from his gathering says: Glory be to You, O God, and praise be to You, I bear witness that there is no god but You, I seek Your forgiveness and turn to You in repentance, will have it as expiation for what occurred in that gathering." A man said: "O Messenger of God! You are saying a saying that you did not used to say before?" He said: "It is an expiation for what happens in the gathering."

The Hafiz Ibn Kathir devoted a separate treatise to this hadith, mentioning its chains, its wordings, and its defects, may God have mercy on him.

It is not hidden that the wording of the verse applies to all the places mentioned, and the hadiths mentioned indicate acting upon its generality, for the Sunnah is an explanation of the Noble Book.

**The discussion on the interpretation of His saying:**

[49] ﴿And during the night, glorify Him, and at the retreat of the stars.﴾

﴿And during the night, glorify Him﴾ means: remember Him and worship Him by reciting (the Qur'an) and praying at night, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And during the night, wake up for prayer as an additional (devotion) for you; it may be that your Lord will raise you to a praised station.﴾ [al-Isra': 79]

[(p-5552)] It has been narrated concerning the remembrances of the night, including the glorifications, what is well known in the books of hadith. I have gathered these, stripped of their chains of transmission, in my book (al-Awrad al-Ma'thurah, "The Transmitted Litanies").

﴿And at the retreat of the stars﴾ means: glorify Him at the time of their retreat, which is their inclining toward setting below the horizon as the light of dawn spreads. This may refer either to the obligatory Fajr prayer or its sunnah prayer, or to what includes both. Qatadah said: "We were told that these are the two rak'ahs at the rising of dawn." It is established in (al-Sahihayn, "the Two Sahih Collections," i.e. al-Bukhari and Muslim) on the authority of 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was never more consistent in any of the supererogatory prayers than in the two rak'ahs of Fajr."

In the wording of Muslim: "The two rak'ahs of Fajr are better than the world and everything in it."

Al-Zamakhshari said: It was also read as ﴿wa-adbara﴾ [Qaf: 40] with a fatha, meaning "in the wake of the stars and their traces when they set."

**Note:**

In (al-Iklil, "The Crown"), citing al-Kirmani, it is said: some jurists used this verse as evidence that performing the Subh prayer during the lightening of dawn (al-isfar) is more excellent, because stars do not "retreat" but only hide from sight. End of quotation.

And this is a sound inference.
